title: interval
content_html:
interval

In train moments, the timestamps mark individual captures while leaving the time between them to the reader. In a film such as by the river, time passes while the viewer looks. A pause between lines in Moments can hold time open in yet another way. An interval can be a gap, a distance or a span in which something happens. What changes in the relation between two images or two lines when more time passes between them? Train moments Work · By the river

Reading note. Daoism. Chapter 16 of the Daodejing puts stillness alongside observing things as they return to their roots. A pause in a poem or film might likewise give us time to recognise a movement already underway. What becomes possible to notice when the interval is long enough? Daodejing, 16
